messages:
maria-sec: Heads-up — customer X asked for an auditable export format for all tenant-level audit events (S3 bundle + signature) and wants SLA language for delivery. Thoughts on feasibility and scope?
raj-infra: Are they asking for a full stream or a point-in-time bundle?
olivia-privacy: They specifically want a forensics pack covering the last 90 days on request. Must include creation/modification events, RBAC grants/revokes, and KMS key-wrapping ops.
maria-sec: Correct. Also they require cryptographic signing of bundles (HSM-backed) and non-repudiation assertions in contract.
sam-runtime: We can generate a zipped bundle with NDJSON events + manifest. Signing: either we sign server-side with our KMS or provide an HSM-signed cert. HSM adds compliance overhead.
anna-legal: From contract perspective customers want an assertion that events are complete up to a given wall-clock. They'll expect delivery within a contractual window (they mentioned 5 business days). Also retention and retention proof needs clarifying.
maria-sec: Key Q: do we support deterministic, immunity-to-tampering export? If we sign with our KMS, customer still has to trust our custody. Some customers want an attestation (signed hash) that can be verified against logs we keep.
raj-infra: Technical concerns: exporting full tenant event sets for 90 days could be large and impact S3 egress/costs. We should consider a sampling/summary option vs full export. Also need to mask PII automatically per privacy rules before export.
olivia-privacy: No PII in audit events ideally. But metadata like username/email may leak. We should include redaction options and a signed statement of redaction steps in the manifest.
sam-runtime: On schema: we need a stable export schema v1 that includes event_id, ts, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource, resource_id, before/after (optional), ksm_key_id_for_encryption_ops, request_id, trace_id, and a signed_manifest with bundle_hash and signing_key_id. Example manifest JSON: ```{\n  "bundle_hash": "sha256:...",\n  "signed_by": "redwood-kms:signing-key-42",\n  "events_count": 12345,\n  "time_range": ["2025-10-01T00:00:00Z","2025-12-31T23:59:59Z"],\n  "redactions": ["email","ip"],\n  "schema_version": "audit_export_v1"\n}```
maria-sec: Good. Also need an 'evidence_chain' field to point at per-event signatures for KMS ops (e.g., when we call customer-managed KMS we should record a wrapped_key_id and KMS-attach signature).
raj-infra: Implementation note: if we include per-event signatures for all events that's costly. Maybe only sign the manifest and keep per-event checksums; and for KMS operations include the KMS response blob (key wrap metadata) as part of event.
olivia-privacy: For HIPAA customers they may need covered entity-level access to audit trails and BAA wording. Anna, legal — can we get sample clause language for "evidence delivery" and custody disclaimers?
anna-legal: I'll draft suggested contract language: define "Audit Evidence Export" (AES) delivered within X business days, scope = account-level events, signed manifest hashed with customer-provided public key (optional). We should offer two modes: (1) Redwood-signed with our KMS (standard) and (2) customer-provided verification key (they upload public key to our control plane) for legal non-repudiation.
maria-sec: That maps to technical: allow customers to register a verification key; when we create bundle we sign using our HSM and also sign bundle_hash with the customer public key? Usually we sign with our private key; customer verifies. If customer supplies a keypair, we can encrypt the bundle and include an envelope.
sam-runtime: We should also document SLA impact: generating a 90-day bundle could be queued as a heavy job. Propose SLA options: standard (7 business days, no charge), expedited (2 business days, fee), emergency forensic (24-72 hours, enterprise add-on + SSO audit).
raj-infra: We'll need rate limits, quotas, and a dedicated job queue with cpu/gpu? no GPU. Also think about retention proof: customers sometimes want proof that events existed at an earlier time. Consider append-only log with periodic signed checkpoints (e.g., Merkle tree root published daily).
maria-sec: Merkle roots published to a timestamping service could provide tamper-evidence. Does infra want to take that on?
raj-infra: We can prototype daily signed checkpoints for tenant-scoped logs. Storage-wise it's small. Ops impact minimal.
olivia-privacy: Also need privacy review on what we publish. The checkpoint must not leak PII. Only use event hashes.
anna-legal: Contract ask: require us to include "chain of custody" appendix that lists who prepared the bundle, redaction steps, and verification steps. Also tie SLA credits to missed delivery windows.
maria-sec: Action items: 1) sam to draft audit_export_v1 schema and signing manifest (due next Tue). 2) raj to scope export job queue + cost estimate (due Fri). 3) anna to draft contract clause options and SLA tiers (due Wed). 4) olivia to write privacy/redaction checklist (due Wed). I'll coordinate with the customer on acceptable delivery windows.
sec-bot: Note added: incident-1234 related forensic export playbook linked -> https://internal/docs/forensics/export-playbook
sam-runtime: Quick Q: should exported manifests include a rolling sequence number for replay detection? I think yes.
maria-sec: Yes include bundle_sequence and export_request_id. Also log the export_request_id as a special audit event in the tenant log.
raj-infra: I'll add a flag to mark export events as high-cost so billing can capture egress.
olivia-privacy: If anyone needs privacy exemptions for on-prem customers, ping me.
anna-legal: I'll follow-up with redlined clause proposals.
maria-sec: Thanks all. We'll recap in next week's compliance sync. :white_check_mark:
